Subject: Streaming endpoint: high-latency affecting interactive sessions (initial notice)

Hi Jamie / Priya —

We’re currently observing elevated end-to-end latency for streaming/chat sessions hitting our streaming endpoint in the us-west region. A subset of interactive sessions are experiencing delayed token emission and intermittent long pauses (10–45s) during generation. We know this is impacting your live support flows and wanted to share what we know and immediate next steps.

Impact observed:
- Affected endpoints: streaming.v1.generate (token-by-token responses)
- Symptom: long pauses / chunked emissions during long-running conversations; some sessions time out and reconnects are required
- Estimated customer impact: 2–7% of active sessions; more pronounced during peak user surges

What we’re doing now (engineers already engaged):
- Triage in progress; switching a small set of serving pods to an alternate batching policy to reduce prefix batching latency
- Rolling a targeted config change to KV cache eviction thresholds in the us-west pool to prevent cache stalls
- Increasing autoscaler capacity for affected shards to absorb bursty traffic patterns

Short-term mitigations you can apply immediately (client-side):
1) If your integration supports it, switch to the synchronous (non-streaming) generate endpoint for critical single-turn flows while we stabilize streaming.
2) Add a lightweight client retry with exponential backoff + jitter for streaming fragmentation; treat short pauses (<30s) as transient and retry the connect.
3) Reduce max_tokens for interactive messages where feasible (shorter replies reduce pressure on the tail token path).
4) If you have a fallback path, enable it to route users to a degraded-but-safe user experience (shorter response, or server-side summary generation).

We’re collecting session traces and will share a timeline and remediation plan in the next 90–120 minutes. Please attach any session_ids you have (example: session_abc123) to the ticket we opened (FE-3072). I’ve attached a diagnostics_request.txt with steps to collect a minimal trace if you can.

Apologies for the disruption — we know live convos are sensitive. I’ll update you with concrete mitigations shortly.

— Hannah

Hannah / team — quick technical summary from triage:
- Preliminary root cause hypothesis: under a particular request-size / concurrency mix the streaming runtime’s continuous batching heuristic held tokens longer than intended while waiting for batch completion; this interacted poorly with a recently tightened KV cache eviction that increased cache misses for longer contexts.
- What we’ve changed:
  * Short-term: shifted affected nodes to the relaxed-batching policy (reduces wait-for-batch time).
  * Applied a hotfix to increase KV cache TTL for active conversation keys to reduce eviction-induced stalls.
  * Scaled up the us-west serving pool by ~25% to absorb immediate bursts.
- Client visible mitigations we recommend to FinEdge:
  1) Add a client-side streaming reconnect after a 12s pause (idempotent reads) with randomized jitter.
  2) Prefer the non-streaming generate for 1:1 single-turn flows during the window.
  3) If using our SDK, set streamingBatchHint to "low-latency" as an interim flag (we’ll publish a small patch with the flag name in the ticket).

I’ll keep monitoring logs for reduced token hold times; next update in ~30 mins.

— Karthik
Senior SRE, Runtime Optimization

Hi Jamie / Priya —

Thanks for the quick confirmation and the session ids. We’ve implemented a few production-side mitigations that should reduce the pauses you’re seeing:
- Serving pool increased and affected nodes switched to a lower-latency batching policy.
- KV cache TTL increased for active conversation keys to avoid eviction-induced stalls.

Immediate client steps (we included a temporary_client_config.yaml attached):
- Toggle: use non-streaming generate for priority queues (critical ticket flows).
- Client retry: reconnect after a 12s pause with exponential backoff and jitter.
- SDK flag: set streamingBatchHint: low-latency (temporary patch/flag will be available in the next hour).

We’ve opened INC-4721 to track the incident and will follow up with a full postmortem and timeline once the triage completes. We’ll also include recommended long-term config changes (kernel/batching defaults and safer KV eviction profiles) to prevent recurrence.

If you can, please confirm when you’ve toggled the priority queues to non-streaming so we can correlate improvement in our telemetry.

Apologies again for the disruption — we’ll stay on this until fully resolved.
